chunks: And in the Nawaadir of Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked

about an Imam leading salat with four people or five, and two declare that they have prayed three, while three declare that they have prayed four. These say, “Stand up,” and these say, “Sit down,” while the Imam inclines toward one of the two sides or is evenly uncertain. So what is obligatory upon them?

He said: “There is no sahw upon the Imam when those behind him preserve for him his sahw by agreement among them; and there is no sahw upon those behind the Imam when the Imam has not erred. And there is no sahw within sahw. And there is no sahw in Maghrib, nor is there sahw in Fajr, nor is there sahw in the first two rakʿahs of every salat.”
So when those behind the Imam differ concerning him, then upon him and upon them is precaution, repetition, and acting upon certainty.”

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs, here the first two units of prayer
key_terms.سَهْوٌ: forgetfulness or mistaken uncertainty in salat

ai.seo_question: What should an Imam and congregation do if they disagree about the number of rakʿahs in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings about sahw in congregational salat, especially when the Imam and followers differ over the number of rakʿahs prayed. It states that agreement of the congregation can preserve the Imam from error, but when the followers themselves disagree, both the Imam and congregation must resort to precaution and repeat the prayer on the basis of certainty.
